concepts.why: The patient has a confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infection and bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT, consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
The patient has bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT and requires mechanical ventilation, consistent with ARDS.
The patient has a high WBC count and elevated CRP, and was started on cefepime for suspected VAP.
The patient has a high WBC count, elevated CRP, and tachycardia, consistent with sepsis.
The patient has a prolonged APTT and elevated D-dimer, consistent with DIC.
The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine on abdominal CT, consistent with intestinal ischemia.
The patient has tachycardia and hypotension, consistent with cardiac dysfunction.
The patient has diffuse edema of the intestine and requires continuous renal replacement therapy, consistent with AKI.

rationales.F01: The patient's symptoms of fever and cough are consistent with COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F02: The confirmation of SARS-CoV-2 infection by nasopharyngeal PCR strongly supports the diagnosis of COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F08: The elevated white blood cell count is consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, such as COVID-19 pneumonia or ARDS.
rationales.F09: The elevated C-reactive protein level is consistent with an infectious or inflammatory process, such as COVID-19 pneumonia or ARDS.
rationales.F10: The presence of bilateral ground-glass opacities with lower-lung predominance on chest CT is highly suggestive of COVID-19 pneumonia.
rationales.F11: The diffuse edema of the intestine, including the transverse colon, may be related to intestinal ischemia or other conditions.
rationales.F12: The prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (APTT) may be indicative of coagulopathy, such as disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC).
